Most of today's home electrical circuits have some component such as an electrolytic capacitor or a transformer with a close-to-free-space antenna that make them suitable for induction cooking because currents at such close-to free-space frequencies are able to pass through their circuits without much obstruction; they're also safe enough at higher currents that they're capable of powering typical induction cooking appliances without causing any overheating.
